alt.en: A sepia photograph of flat, open grassland running to a low, level horizon under a pale, empty sky, with patches of bare ground, a few small grazing animals far off and one dark animal grazing near the right edge.
alt.es: Fotografía en tono sepia de una pradera llana y abierta que se extiende hasta un horizonte bajo y recto bajo un cielo pálido y vacío, con manchas de tierra desnuda, unos pocos animales pastando a lo lejos y uno oscuro pastando cerca del borde derecho.

caption.en: The open Kansas plains near Monument, photographed about 1867 for the railway survey published as Across the Continent on the Kansas Pacific Railroad, a few years before Higley took up his homestead in Smith County in 1871.
caption.es: Las llanuras abiertas de Kansas cerca de Monument, fotografiadas hacia 1867 para el estudio ferroviario publicado como Across the Continent on the Kansas Pacific Railroad, pocos años antes de que Higley se instalara como colono en el condado de Smith en 1871.

source: On the Great Plains, in Kansas, near Monument, 385 miles west of Missouri River (Across the Continent on the Kansas Pacific Railroad: Route of the 35th Parallel, plate No. 41), albumen print, photographer Alexander Gardner (1821-1882)
library: Boston Public Library, Photographs of the American West (via Digital Commonwealth)
licenceEvidence: Library record: "No known copyright restrictions." / "No known restrictions on use." / rights statement "No Copyright - United States" (http://rightsstatements.org/vocab/NoC-US/1.0/). Photographed about 1867, issued about 1869; Gardner died 1882 (see rights.md).
credit: Boston Public Library, Alexander Gardner, plate No. 41

alt.en: A colour photograph of a small one-room cabin with a steep shingled roof: the front wall is of pale, squared logs with a plank door and a small window, and the gable end is of stone. A wooden bench stands by the wall, and the cabin sits on mown grass among tall trees under a blue sky.
alt.es: Fotografía en color de una pequeña cabaña de una sola habitación con un tejado empinado de tablillas: la pared delantera es de troncos claros escuadrados, con una puerta de tablones y una ventana pequeña, y el hastial es de piedra. Junto a la pared hay un banco de madera, y la cabaña se alza sobre césped cortado entre árboles altos, bajo un cielo azul.

caption.en: Higley's later home on West Beaver Creek in Smith County, a log cabin, photographed in 2014: it replaced the dugout he lived in when he wrote the poem, and the dugout is gone.
caption.es: La casa posterior de Higley junto a West Beaver Creek, en el condado de Smith, una cabaña de troncos, fotografiada en 2014: sustituyó a la vivienda excavada en la tierra donde vivía cuando escribió el poema, y esa vivienda ya no existe.

source: Home on the Range cabin from SE 1 (Home on the Range Cabin, Smith County, Kansas, seen from the southeast, 4 September 2014)

alt.en: A narrow column of old newspaper print headed "PLAGIARISM.", a paragraph of small type, then a poem headed "Western Home." and "BY DR. HIGLEY." beginning "Oh! give me a home where the Buffalo roam, Where the Deer and the Antelope play; Where never is heard a discouraging word", followed by its chorus.
alt.es: Una columna estrecha de un periódico antiguo con el título "PLAGIARISM.", un párrafo en letra pequeña y luego un poema titulado "Western Home." y "BY DR. HIGLEY.", que empieza "Oh! give me a home where the Buffalo roam, Where the Deer and the Antelope play; Where never is heard a discouraging word", seguido de su estribillo.

caption.en: From the Kirwin Chief's front page of 26 February 1876: under "PLAGIARISM" the paper credits the poem to "Dr. B. Higley, of Beaver creek" and reprints it as Western Home, the earliest copy Kirke Mechem could find.
caption.es: De la primera página del Kirwin Chief del 26 de febrero de 1876: bajo "PLAGIARISM" (plagio), el periódico atribuye el poema al "Dr. B. Higley, of Beaver creek" y lo vuelve a publicar como Western Home, la copia más antigua que pudo encontrar Kirke Mechem.

source: The Kirwin Chief (Kirwin, Kansas), vol. 3, 26 February 1876, front page, first column ("PLAGIARISM" and "Western Home"), as reproduced in Kirke Mechem, "Home on the Range", The Kansas Historical Quarterly 17, no. 4 (November 1949), plate between pp. 328 and 329
library: Kansas State Historical Society (original issue); Internet Archive microfilm scan of The Kansas Historical Quarterly
licenceEvidence: Newspaper printed 26 February 1876 (anonymous editor; poem by Higley, died 1911). The crop shows only the 1876 page as photographically reproduced in 1949, none of the 1949 journal's own text; a faithful reproduction of a flat public-domain page adds no new copyright (see rights.md).
credit: The Kirwin Chief, 26 February 1876, as reproduced in The Kansas Historical Quarterly (1949), via the Internet Archive

alt.en: A printed page of music headed "Home on the Range", in three flats and 6/8 time: three systems, each a voice line with words over two piano staves, the words reading "Oh, give me a home where the buf-fa-lo roam, Where the deer and the an-te-lope play; Where sel-dom is heard a dis-cour-ag-ing word".
alt.es: Página impresa de música con el título "Home on the Range", con tres bemoles y en 6/8: tres sistemas, cada uno con una línea de canto con la letra sobre dos pentagramas de piano; la letra dice "Oh, give me a home where the buf-fa-lo roam, Where the deer and the an-te-lope play; Where sel-dom is heard a dis-cour-ag-ing word".

caption.en: The tune in John Lomax's Cowboy Songs and Other Frontier Ballads (New York, November 1910), as Henry Lebermann took it down from Lomax's 1908 San Antonio recording, printed with no author or composer named.
caption.es: La melodía en Cowboy Songs and Other Frontier Ballads de John Lomax (Nueva York, noviembre de 1910), tal como Henry Lebermann la transcribió de la grabación que Lomax hizo en San Antonio en 1908, impresa sin nombre de autor ni de compositor.

source: John A. Lomax, ed., Cowboy Songs and Other Frontier Ballads (New York: Sturgis & Walton, published November 1910), "Home on the Range", music, first page (unnumbered leaf after p. 40)
library: University of Toronto, Robarts Library (digitized by the Internet Archive)
licenceEvidence: "Copyright 1910 By Sturgis & Walton Company ... Published November, 1910" (verso of title page). Lomax died 1948, Lebermann 1941, Higley 1911, Kelley 1905; IA record: possible-copyright-status NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT (see rights.md).
